claims.reason: [Finite ι] is an argument: it is an instance-implicit variable and ι is pulled in by M, c and u. The statement elaborates the same without it. DifferentiableOn only needs AddCommGroup/Module/TopologicalSpace (FDeriv/Defs.lean, lines 96-97), and the topology on ContinuousMultilinearMap 𝕜 M H is the general instTopologicalSpace (Topology/Algebra/Module/Multilinear/Topology.lean), which assumes nothing about ι. The normed instances need Fintype ι, which [Finite ι] does not supply as an instance, so the current statement already uses the general structures. The only [Finite ι] instance in the Multilinear files is the Prop-valued instContinuousEval, which the statement does not use. The statement stays true and the proposed proof works. `ContinuousMultilinearMap.apply 𝕜 E F m : _ →L[𝕜] F` (Topology.lean, line 318) needs only ContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 F, IsTopologicalAddGroup F and ContinuousSMul 𝕜 (E i), all available here, and no finiteness. HasFDerivAtFilter is a structure with field `isLittleOTVS` and constructor `of_isLittleOTVS` (Defs.lean, lines 110-112). `ContinuousLinearMap.isBigOTVS_comp` (Asymptotics/TVS.lean, line 421) and `IsBigOTVS.trans_isLittleOTVS` (line 293) hold for any topological vector spaces over a nontrivially normed field. Composing evaluation at u with the little-o bound for c gives HasFDerivWithinAt (fun y ↦ c y u) ((apply 𝕜 M H u) ∘L c') s x; the two difference functions agree pointwise because evaluation is linear. Hence DifferentiableOn holds for arbitrary ι.
